newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to open Credit Lyonnais aid probe - EU source.
newsitem.headline: EU to open Credit Lyonnais aid probe - EU source.

text.p: The European Commission is expected on Wednesday to open a state aid probe into the purchase by troubled French bank Credit Lyonnais of Societe de Banque Occidentale (SDBO), a European Union source said on Friday.

"We're raising a series of questions on this specific element of the (Credit Lyonnais) restructuring plan," the source said, referring to the 45-billion-franc French government rescue plan which the Commission approved with conditions last year.
"There might be elements of state aid, we believe, in the way it (the purchase) has happened," the source added.

SDBO was a Credit Lyonnais unit before being transferred to the Consortium de Realisation (CDR) asset-sale body, the government body created to sell the bank's assets as part of the rescue plan. But in February Credit Lyonnais said it had signed a pact to take back the assets and staff of SDBO from CDR.
The source said the expected inquiry would concern the way the acquisition had taken place, at what price and the way it had been handled by CDR.
"It is the conditions under which they bought it back that we have questions about," the source said.

Credit Lyonnais, whose downfall was the biggest banking scandal in recent French history, lost 21 billion francs between 1992 and 1994 as a result of a reckless expansion binge before eking out a slim 13 million franc profit in 1995.
On Thursday, the Commission denied a newspaper report that it had received a letter from the French government outlining plans to soften the terms of last year's state rescue.
A spokesman said the Commission had received a letter from Finance Minister Jean Arthuis about the troubled state- controlled bank but that he had not made any reference to a new recovery plan.
